docs.title: Flashback Actors
docs.text:
A Fabric addon for Flashback that records actors inside a replay. Enter actor mode, perform a take, stop: the performance plays back on the timeline as a clone, and you act against it on the next take.

  • :material-movie-open:{ .lg .middle } Record takes

    Press R, perform, press R. Chases and fights are multiple passes.

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: How takes work

  • :material-download:{ .lg .middle } Install

    Fabric Loader, Fabric API, Flashback, and the matching jar.

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: Install guide

  • :material-palette:{ .lg .middle } Dress the cast

    Emotes, gear, morphs, and skins, all resolved per tick without re-recording.

  • :material-video:{ .lg .middle } Direct it

    Director presets, shot lists, a monitor wall, and full timeline ops.

Not the first word on actors

The idea of an actor in Flashback is not new: see Flashback Studio and Flashback Actor Replay.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Take-format versions are the compatibility contract: a take file records the version that wrote it, newer builds read older files, and older builds refuse newer files at the version check.

docs.title: Unreleased
docs.text:
• Take format v28: sound cues. Performer-caused playSound broadcasts are recorded (id, position, volume, pitch, source) and rebroadcast on playback; block breaks replay the vanilla destroy event for particles plus sound.
  • Take format v27: ride transitions. Mounts and dismounts record the vehicle identity; clones re-board the same entity.
  • Container recording enabled: slot, open, and close capture mixins registered; block-entity pre-break capture retargeted to Level.
  • Chest playback: correct menu type per block entity, lid animation, open and close sounds across all nine targets.
  • Watermark licence notice, logged once at startup.
  • Public CI (static checks) and a self-hosted release workflow.

Full history: CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Install Fabric Loader 0.16+ and Fabric API for your game version.
  2. Install Flashback (0.39+, 0.42+ on 26.x).
  3. Download the matching jar from GitHub releases into mods.
  4. Java 21 runs the 1.21.x jars; the 26.x jars need Java 25.

docs.title: Record takes
docs.text:
1. Open a replay in Flashback and scrub to where the actor enters.
  2. Press R (or the actor track's New actor take row). The editor hides itself, playback rolls after a 3-2-1 countdown, and you perform in survival.
  3. Perform. Breaking and placing blocks is real; each edit is recorded against its tick. (Editing is refused during setup, when the level is still scrubbing.)
  4. Press R to stop. You return to spectator and the playhead jumps back to where the take started.

Takes live per replay under flashback/fbactors/<replay-uuid>/<take-uuid>.take. Nothing is written into the .flashback file, so replays open normally without this mod.

docs.title: What a take remembers
docs.text: Body and held items, combat (measured strikes, health, effects, arrows), world edits (blocks with drops and sounds, mining overlays, block-entity data, containers, vehicle rides, performer-caused sounds), and optional voice.

docs.title: Sharing takes
docs.text: /actor bundle export writes every take plus gear and emote slices into one <replay>.fbactors.zip beside the replay file; /actor bundle import (or just opening a replay whose bundle sits beside it) brings the cast back.

docs.title: Take format versions
docs.text: The format is append-only: newer builds read older takes, older builds refuse newer ones at the version check. Current version: v28 (sound cues), v27 added rides. Full history lives in CHANGELOG.md.
